context_build.causal_mechanism: After a delivered Fed hike, US overnight and 2Y yields sit well above Canada. Canada can catch up some through the already-steeper CORRA path; that would also profit a short CA-US_2Y. The energy-pass-through BoC-hike narrative is the catalyst that would overwhelm carry; the 16 Sep Saudi Oman workaround reduced that oil-supply tail.

The energy-hike catalyst that would overwhelm this is weaker after the Saudi Oman workaround, not stronger. Unknowns: NZ rates, CFTC, live temperature-gauge vintages. The discrepancy lives in the 2Y yield gap (-140bp, 1y percentile 3.77, 5y percentile 4.31), not in USDCAD (1y percentile 74.0, z 0.80). Oil/energy cross-currents (Saudi STS workaround versus weakened shock absorbers and BoC energy pass-through minutes) contaminate CAD spot. US and CA policy paths are both status ok, so the short-end RV is executable from the frozen packet. Long USDCAD has similar carry but extra ToT/oil residual and is not the stretched object.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Long USDCAD at packet ECB as_of mid 1.4010471204188482 on 2026-09-18; overnight differential SOFR 3.85 versus CORRA 2.29.

trade.horizon: 3 months (patient carry; packet analogs report 1m and 3m forward outcomes)
trade.invalidation: Thesis is invalid if the CORRA path re-prices more tightening than the SOFR path such that the sourced Dec implied gap (SR3Z6 4.32 versus COAZ26 2.58) and the sourced 140bp CA-US_2Y differential compress from the Canada side because energy pass-through overwhelms Canada's core-near-2% and labor-38 setup; or if the Fed tightening bias evidenced by the 16 Sep hike and August CPI is reversed while Canada remains the low-yielder only because US yields collapse. A further analog-style cheapening without path compression is timing noise, not automatic invalidation, because carry is the holding-period engine. No numeric stop is sourced in the packet.
trade.mispricing: The fade of CA-US_2Y at -140bp is the mispricing: it treats a 5y 4th-percentile yield gap as a long-Canada duration signal while the policy path still pays ~149bp to receive US versus pay CA, and while Dec CORRA at 2.58% has not caught a delivered US hike that lifted SOFR to 3.85% and SR3 Dec to 4.32%. Statistical cheapness of CA versus US is the discovery flag, not a reason to own negative carry.
principal_risks: US inflation/labor gauges stay hot and US 2Y rises further versus a capped CA 2Y, driving CA-US_2Y more negative and marking a short RV against the holder; US 2Y is already at the 99.8th 1y percentile.
BoC energy pass-through becomes the binding catalyst (headline 3% plus a renewed oil shock) and CORRA/CA 2Y catch up faster than US carry can cushion.

Positioning is unknown (CFTC/CME unavailable); a crowded short-CAD-rates or long-USDCAD book could amplify a squeeze. Temperature gauges are repo-retained dashboard_v8. NZ rates missing. Paper MTM on rates_rv is duration-1 spread change and does not mechanically credit coupon carry.
trade.structure: Pay CA 2Y versus receive US 2Y; book as short CA-US_2Y (CA minus US). Paper family is sovereign 2Y RV marked from market_state.rate_rv.CA-US_2Y, not SOFR/CORRA futures. Research/reference mids only; not a broker structure.
trade.thesis: Verified fact: US 2Y 4.76% versus CA 2Y 3.27% is a -140bp CA-US_2Y print after a delivered Fed hike and SOFR 3.85% reset, while CORRA overnight is still 2.29% and Dec 1m CORRA is only 2.58%. Inference: the market is inviting a negative-carry fade of Canada cheapness. Carry-is-king will not pay 3.27% to short 4.76%. Short CA-US_2Y receives the high yielder, pays the low yielder, and still has room for Canada to catch up along its own CORRA path. The energy-hike catalyst that would overwhelm this is weaker after the Saudi Oman workaround, not stronger. Unknowns: NZ rates, CFTC, live temperature-gauge vintages. Patient 3-month hold; paper books pay SOFR on the full $100m whether flat or not, so a 149bp yield gap that can also mean-revert from -140bp is a better use of the allocation than sitting flat.
why_now: Fed hike delivered 16 Sep 2026 to 3.75-4.00% after >90% pricing; SOFR effective 17 Sep is 3.85% rather than the 3.62% 16 Sep print, so the overnight hurdle and the US leg have actually reset.
CA-US_2Y printed -140bp on 17 Sep after -139bp on hike day, a fresh 1m -17bp cheapening, while CORRA Oct is still only +1.5bp and Dec 1m only +29bp.

Saudi STS workaround 16 Sep reduced the extreme oil-supply tail that would have been the catalyst capable of overwhelming carry via a BoC energy hike; empty $100m seed pays official SOFR ACT/360 every calendar day even if flat.

events.rationale: Verified: SOFR 3.85% (2026-09-17), CORRA 2.29%, AONIA 4.35%; Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep after >90% futures odds; CA-US 2Y is -140bp as of 17 Sep. Inference: the 149bp US-over-Canada 2Y yield gap is the holding-period engine, not a fade. Unknown: CFTC/CME positioning and NZ rates. Patient expression is pay CA 2Y / receive US 2Y (short CA-US_2Y). Long USDCAD is the spot alternative; rates own the discrepancy more cleanly.

holes_in_opposing_case: perma-bull is the only USD-down pitch in this bundle and it does not own a markable NZ policy path. NZ rates are a frozen known gap, so long NZDUSD cannot show whether the seat is paid to wait against SOFR 3.85 after a delivered Fed hike. A 0.2% q/q GDP beat and an India FTA covering ~95% of NZ exports are not a new overnight-funding transmission; labor 32 and consumer 38 remain the packet's NZ cyclical state. CAD higher is a sidecar tag with no CAD instrument.

value-guy shares short CA-US_2Y but converts the same 4th-percentile 2Y gap into CAD higher. That FX leap is not in the rates mark: 2027-09 STIR still leaves SOFR 4.755 versus CORRA 3.51 (124.5bp), and overnight remains 3.85 versus 2.29. A 3m analog of +25bp from -145bp still leaves a triple-digit gap. Energy pass-through is their closer; the 16 Sep Saudi STS workaround reduced that oil-supply tail. Percentile is their discovery flag being asked to do FX work it cannot do.

rate-dove and perma-bear receive 2027 CORRA (3.365 / 3.51 implied versus overnight 2.29). That is the negative-carry fade this seat refuses: long the low-yielder after the Fed has already reset SOFR to 3.85 while Dec 1m CORRA is only 2.58. Labor 38 and core-near-2% cap how far Canada can hike; they do not justify receiving CA duration against a 149bp 2Y pickup the other way. perma-bear even tags carry as opposing its own trade.

rate-hawk and trend-follower pay SR3U7 4.755. That is the exciting low-carry US-hike narrative: known heat (72/75/69/74) plus a hike that was already >90% priced. Known information needs a new transmission to justify paying the peak. Carry of paying 4.755 versus overnight 3.85 is negative if the extra 90.5bp is not delivered. Their US-rates-up risk is already my principal risk on the receive-US leg; it is not a reason to switch into paying SOFR.

dollar-king's long USDCAD agrees on USD up / CAD down but locates the edge in a 74th-percentile pair that I already rejected as the stretched object. Oil ToT (Saudi workaround versus weakened shock absorbers) contaminates CAD spot. EURUSD/USDCHF having 'already moved' is not a closing mechanism for USDCAD. The 2Y gap is the discrepancy; spot is the residual.

mean-reverter's USD-up tag has no USD expression and CAD is not_relevant, so it does not rebut my CAD view. Receiving AONIA_2026-10 fades 21.5bp of priced RBA hikes after housing evidence I already inspected and declined as a primary because AU inflation 82 versus a housing catalyst is two-sided.

attack: Strongest opposing claim on the routed USD/CAD conflicts: perma-bull that NZDUSD is the cheap cyclical and therefore USD should be lower and CAD higher. That claim has no NZ carry or NZ policy path in the freeze, fights a just-delivered US hike and hot US gauges, and treats a 5y-cheap NZD after -3.90% 1m as a pro-growth entry. Carry will not fund that.

Second opposing claim: value-guy that short CA-US_2Y implies CAD higher via BoC catch-up. Same rates direction, wrong FX mapping. CA rates can rise relative to US without CAD outrunning the 156bp overnight gap. Their closer is the energy-hike catalyst my original invalidation already names, and the packet's Saudi workaround made that catalyst weaker, not stronger.

The CORRA-receive camp (rate-dove, perma-bear) is the economic opposite of paying CA 2Y. They ask the book to own more Canada cheapness after SOFR has already jumped to 3.85 and CA-US_2Y has already printed -140bp. That is the fade I will not pay 3.27% to own.

The SOFR-pay camp (rate-hawk, trend-follower) overpays for a terminal debate the strip already has at 4.755. I receive US 2Y at 4.76 because that is where the holding-period return lives, not because I need US yields to collapse.
defense: Original stands: short CA-US_2Y, pay CA 2Y 3.27 / receive US 2Y 4.76, packet mid -140bp as of 2026-09-17. USD higher and CAD lower remain the FX implication of that rate differential until a Canada-side energy re-pricing overwhelms it. I do not amend into long NZDUSD, long CAD, receive CORRA, or pay SOFR.
Rates still beat spot. Dollar-king's USDCAD case is my already-constructed spot candidate; oil residual and a non-extreme 74th-percentile print keep the edge in the 2Y RV.

Uncertainty preserved: CFTC/CME positioning is unavailable; temperature gauges are dashboard_v8; NZ rates are missing; paper MTM on rates_rv does not mechanically credit coupon. Mixed 3m analogs (2025-01-30 +25bp versus 2024-12-18 -20bp) cap confidence at 58.

What would concede: CORRA/CA 2Y re-prices more tightening than SOFR/US 2Y from the Canada side because energy pass-through overwhelms core-near-2% and labor 38, or the Fed tightening bias reverses and US yields collapse while Canada stays the low-yielder only as a US rally. A further analog-style cheapening without that path compression is timing noise, not a flip to receive CA.
